verdict.rationale: Filee's conversion engines run entirely on the user's own machines: it is offline, MIT open source, buildable on Linux, and installable silently or as a portable ZIP. A documented CLI (`filee convert` with `--json` output and exit codes) lets scripts on hosts you operate drive those engines. However, nothing documents a library/SDK, container image or server/API mode, and the OpenAPI probes all returned 404. Missing for 10: an embeddable library or SDK, an official container image, a self-hosted server/API mode, and independent corroboration of headless server deployment.

support.subject: As a developer, the conversion engine runs inside my own infrastructure as a library, container, or server I operate

citations.quote: Nothing is uploaded. Filee works offline, so private documents, photos and recordings never leave your computer.
"filee convert <files, wildcards or folders> --to <format>" (or "--preset <preset>") converts with the app's engines and presets
"--json" prints the result for scripts; exit codes are 0 (nothing failed), 1 (some files failed), 2 (wrong arguments or a missing input) and 3 (nothing to convert).
Build with the .NET 10 SDK on Windows, macOS or Linux
If you can't install programs, use the portable ZIP: unzip it anywhere and run Filee.exe.
